body.statement: If the entries of \(P\), \(c\), and a queried \(\Delta\) are real algebraic, then membership in either \(\Theta_{\mathrm w}(P)\) or \(\Theta_{+}(P)\), projection onto \(c\) or \(\Delta\), the algebraic endpoint values, and their inclusion flags are decided by a terminating real-closed-field quantifier-elimination procedure applied to the principal-minor form of the finite lift.
body.justification: The finite representation yields an exact decision procedure even on singular and weakly infeasible faces.
body.gap: Existing implementations use slope grids and numerical convex solvers; no exact algebraic membership and endpoint-inclusion result is stated for the feedback model.
body.consumer: It provides a correctness benchmark for certified solvers and eliminates arbitrary support and slope grids for algebraically encoded inputs.
body.proof_tex:
For \(v\in\{\mathrm w,+\}\), let \(F_v(P,c,d,z_v)\) denote the conjunction of
the cell equations, the APE equation with value \(d\), the inequality
\(c>0\), and all matrix constraints defining the corresponding lift.  By
\(\mathrm{lem{:}principal\text{-}minor\text{-}psd}\), each matrix constraint
is equivalent to nonnegativity of finitely many principal minors.  The
coefficients of \(A_{xz,yw}\), \(N_c\), \(H_s\), \(K_s\), and \(R_s\) are
polynomials with integer coefficients in \(c\) and the displayed variables.
Thus \(F_v\) is a first-order formula in the language of ordered fields.

On the maintained positive-cell domain,
\(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\text{-}feedback\text{-}cone}\) gives the exact
membership test
\[
 (\log c,d)\in\Theta_v(P)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists z_v\,F_v(P,c,d,z_v). \tag{4}
\]
Existentially eliminating \(z_v\), and then eliminating either \(c\) or
\(d\) while retaining \(c>0\), gives the two requested projections.  The
terminating elimination is supplied by
\(\mathrm{lem{:}real\text{-}closed\text{-}field\text{-}elimination}\).

For completeness, a finite lower endpoint \(\ell\) is characterized entirely
in the same language by
\[
 \begin{split}
 &\exists d,z_v\ F_v(P,c,d,z_v),\\
 &\forall d,z_v\ \bigl(F_v(P,c,d,z_v)\Rightarrow \ell\le d\bigr),\\
 &\forall\epsilon\ \bigl(\epsilon>0\Rightarrow
   \exists d,z_v\,[F_v(P,c,d,z_v)\wedge d<\ell+\epsilon]\bigr).
 \end{split} \tag{5}
\]
The upper formula reverses the inequalities.  Finiteness follows from the
bound in \(\mathrm{thm{:}fixed\text{-}slope\text{-}endpoints}\).  After
quantifier elimination, a one-dimensional definable set is described by
finitely many polynomial sign conditions over the real algebraic input
field; every finite boundary point, hence \(\ell\) and the upper endpoint, is
a root of one of those polynomials and is real algebraic.  Finally, endpoint
inclusion is the separate existential sentence
\(\exists z_vF_v(P,c,\ell,z_v)\), or its upper analogue.  Applying the same
terminating procedure decides its truth.  This proves membership, projection,
endpoint value, and inclusion claims, including singular or infeasible
branches; it makes no complexity claim and introduces no grid in \(c\).
